digest.component_or_area: LLM model class resolution and provider qualification
propositions: A model class configured with provider='bedrock' and a canonical versioned Bedrock id containing a colon in the version suffix (e.g. 'anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0') silently discards the configured provider because the colon test mistakenly treats the version suffix colon as a provider separator.

The _resolve_target function uses 'if ":" in model' to detect provider-qualified strings, but this fails for versioned Bedrock ids where the colon is internal to the model identifier, not a separator, causing the function to return the bare model and discard an explicit provider argument.
An explicitly configured provider must be checked first before scanning the model string for qualifiers, so no punctuation in a model id can overrule or discard a configured provider instruction.
A conflicting pair of inline qualifier and configured provider must raise an error rather than silently picking a winner, since either choice discards an explicit instruction.

The qualified/unqualified decision must be centralized in one shared function (split_provider_qualifier) that both _resolve_target and infer_provider use, so they cannot drift apart and produce different answers for the same input.
